bibl.title: Reading the Citizenship Papyrus (P.Giss. 40)
bibl.seg: Ari Z. Bryen, Reading the Citizenship Papyrus (P.Giss. 40)
Clifford Ando (ed.), Citizenship and Empire in Europe 200-1900. The Antonine Constitution after 1800 Year = Potsdamer Altertumswissenschaftliche Beiträge. 54 (Stuttgart, 2016) pp. 29-43.
bibl.note: Traces two competing understandings of the nature of citizenship in the Roman world, as they appear in P. Giss. I, 40, the papyrus which preserves the text of the Constitutio Antoniniana as well as two other edicts. Argues that state / official understandings of the nature of universal citizenship were difficult to impose, because they met with powerful processes of translation or transformation at the local level.
